0.reason: An open operation means a peer is mid-merge, so the coordinator must wait for it regardless of other refusals; with the refusal now in seconds, a retry that reports the rest costs seconds, not a full promotion.

findings.text: non-blocking: the early refusal runs outside `_require_independently` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1356), so a run whose checkout has an open operation and also fails another independent check now reports only the open operation where the base reported every refusal in one message, costing one further full promotion attempt to learn the rest.

non-blocking: `_landing_checkout` restates the mount-then-record-repo resolution that promotion.py:457 and promotion.py:589 already carry; three copies can drift, and a drift would have the early check name a different checkout than the landing commit writes into.

non-blocking: the recorded gate covers the ledger/store counters, the negative control and the importer delta, but the plan section's timing measure (five calls at base and five at head on all_debug, median wall time under 30 s, each logged with its load average) was never run, so the latency half of the deliverable is asserted from the counters alone.
